meta.title: Insulation Planner - US research dataset
conventions: Every numeric value is accompanied (at row/object level) by 'src' (source id(s) in 'sources') and 'confidence' (high|medium|low).
Fields ending in '_computed' are arithmetic on sourced numbers (e.g., R / thickness), not values printed by the source.
null = could not be verified; see the adjacent 'note'.
products is grouped by type: batts[], loose_fill[] (coverage charts), rigid_boards[], spray_foam{}. prices[] holds individual observations; price_summary[] is computed low/high per product.
products.batts[].framing_spacing_in_o_c is derived from batt width (15/15.25/16 in -> 16 in o.c.; 23/23.25/24 in -> 24 in o.c.) per DOE Building America (source ba_basement_2012).
caveats: Home Depot and Lowe's product pages returned 403/Access Denied to automated fetches and browsers. Their prices here come from search-result snippets with unknown snapshot dates (medium/low confidence). Menards prices were read from live pages on 2026-10-14 (high).
The web-search budget for this research was exhausted before CertainTeed loose-fill charts, a waste-factor source, and a 15 sq ft window-deduction source could be located.
Model codes are adopted (and amended) state by state; IECC values are model-code values.
GreenFiber cellulose charts are in transition (2015 INS-coded labels vs. 2026 SANCTUARY); always prefer the chart printed on the bag being sold.

code.table: Table R402.1.3 Insulation Minimum R-Values and Fenestration Requirements by Component (prescriptive)
notes: R-values are minimums. Where insulation is installed in a cavity that is less than the label or design thickness, the installed R-value must still be at least the table value (PNNL footnote text for 2012-2021 IECC).
Notation 'A+Bci': first value is cavity insulation, second is continuous insulation (ci); e.g. '13+5ci' = R-13 cavity plus R-5 continuous (2021 IECC footnote g, per PNNL).

Notation 'Xci or Y' (basement/crawl space walls): R-X continuous insulation on the interior or exterior surface of the wall OR R-Y cavity insulation on the interior side of the wall. '15ci or 19 or 13+5ci' adds the option R-13 cavity plus R-5 ci.

Mass wall 'A/B': first value applies when more than half the insulation is on the exterior, second value applies when more than half of the insulation is on the interior of the mass wall (2021 IECC footnote h, per PNNL).
Basement wall insulation is not required in warm-humid locations as defined by IECC Figure R301.1 / Table R301.1.
Many states and cities adopt the IECC with amendments, or still enforce an older edition; the calculator should label these as 'model code' targets.
The 'R-30' cavity-only option for wood-frame walls in zones 4-8 was added by ICC erratum (MN DLI worksheet: '30 is added in the erratum'); the DOE energy.gov summary table omits it.
code.zone0_note: Climate Zone 0 was introduced in the 2021 IECC. The PNNL comparison table and the DOE/ENERGY STAR tables start at Zone 1. In the 2021 IECC, Zone 0 shares the 'Zones 0 and 1' requirements; that combined-row reading could not be verified from a fetched copy of the ICC text (the ICC site is JavaScript-rendered and blocked automated fetches), so Zone 0 rows carry medium confidence.
code.wood_frame_wall_numeric_explanation: The calculator needs one 'total R' number, but the code allows several equivalent wall assemblies. 'numeric_r' is the cavity-only option listed in the table (R-13 in zones 0-2, R-20 in zone 3, R-30 in zones 4-8), which is the one a homeowner filling an existing stud cavity can compare against directly. Do NOT add cavity + ci nominal values and compare across options: the code treats R-20+5ci (nominal sum 25), R-13+10ci (23) and R-0+20ci (20) as equivalent to R-30 cavity-only because continuous insulation is not interrupted by studs (no thermal bridging). Note also that a 2x4 cavity (3.5 in) holds at most about R-15 of batts and a 2x6 cavity (5.5 in) about R-21 to R-23, so zone 3-8 targets generally require 2x6 framing plus continuous insulation in practice. 'nominal_sums' lists the arithmetic sum of each option for reference only.

basement_wall.note: Not required in warm-humid locations (IECC Figure R301.1).

wood_frame_wall.note: '30 or' option added by erratum; pre-erratum printing and the DOE summary list only 20+5ci or 13+10ci or 0+20ci.

summary: Table R402.1.3 updated: window and skylight efficiencies updated, ceiling insulation requirements decreased (NEEP summary does not give the new values), and an option added to use continuous insulation for framed floors; values for insulation entirely above the roof deck added.
New Section R402.2.3 Attic Knee Walls with specific insulation requirements.
Prescriptive air leakage tightened to 2.5 ACH50 in Climate Zones 6-8.

R408 Additional Efficiency Requirements rewritten as a points/credit system (insulation, windows, HVAC, water heating, air sealing, ventilation, ducts); additions and alterations to existing buildings must also select credits (R502.2.5, R503.1.5).
New Appendix RF: Alternative Building Thermal Envelope Insulation R-Value Options.

unverified_claim.text: A Cochise County (AZ) supplemental summary states the 2024 IECC reduced the Climate Zone 3 ceiling requirement from R-49 back to R-38. Not corroborated by a primary source in this research; that document also contains other statements that appear inaccurate.

changes_2024_iecc.note: NEEP's summary describes the consensus-committee draft (Dec 2023). Check the final 2024 IECC Table R402.1.3 before using any 2024 numbers.

recommended.title: ENERGY STAR Recommended Home Insulation R-Values: recommended insulation levels for retrofitting existing wood-framed buildings
recommended.basis: ENERGY STAR states the guidance is based on 2021 IECC Residential Provisions Chapter 4 Table R402.1.3.
recommended.attic_column_meaning: The second attic column is the R-value to ADD when 3-4 inches of insulation already exist (the table header reads 'Add Insulation to Attic ... If you already have 3-4 inches of insulation').
recommended.wall_text: Wall Insulation (above the ground) - Whenever exterior siding is removed on an: Uninsulated wood-frame wall: Drill holes in the sheathing and blow insulation into the empty wall cavity before installing the new siding, and Zone 3: Add R5 insulative wall sheathing beneath the new siding; Zones 4-8: Add R5 to R10 insulative wall sheathing beneath the new siding. OR Insulated 2x4 wood-frame wall: For Zones 4-8: Add R10 insulative wall sheathing beneath the new siding.
recommended.basement_crawlspace_wall_text: Basement or Crawlspace Wall Insulation: Zone 3: Add R5 insulative wall sheathing or R13 batt. Zones 4A and 4B: Add R10 insulative wall sheathing or R13 batt. Zones 4C and 5-8: Add R15 insulative wall sheathing or R19 batt.
recommended.zone0_note: ENERGY STAR's table starts at Zone 1; no Zone 0 row is published.

rule_of_thumb.text: ENERGY STAR 'Ask the Experts' (Feb 2, 2024): Southern U.S. minimum R-38 or about 13-14 inches; Northern U.S. minimum R-49 or about 16-18 inches; most common types have R-3 to R-3.5 per inch; add insulation if levels are more than 4-6 inches below the recommended level.

materials.name: Fiberglass batts/rolls (new)
materials.note: For new batts use the labelled product R-value (see products.batts). Per-inch varies with density: computed from manufacturer sheets 2.92 (R-19 at 6.5 in) to 4.29 (R-15 at 3.5 in). 3.2 is ENERGY STAR's multiplier for fiberglass batts, a reasonable generic value. Knauf: 'When R-19 6.25" is installed in a 2 x 6 cavity, the R-value will be R-18.'

materials.name: Mineral wool / stone wool batts (new)
materials.note: Building America basement guide gives R-3 to 4 per inch for mineral wool; Building America wall guide gives approx. R-3.7/in for rigid mineral wool. ROCKWOOL Comfortbatt computes to 3.71 (R-13), 4.29 (R-15), 3.82 (R-21), 4.18 (R-23), 4.14 (R-30), 4.0 (R-38). 4.2 is a rounded value for the R-15/R-23/R-30 line; prefer the labelled R-value.

materials.name: Loose-fill (blown) fiberglass (new)
materials.note: Computed as R / minimum settled thickness from the manufacturer charts in products.loose_fill (rows R-19 and up). For new installs use the product chart thickness directly, never a generic per-inch value. Building America wall guide: 'Depending on installation density, loose fill cellulose and fiberglass can provide insulation values of R-3.6-R-3.8/in.' (dense-pack wall context).
materials.use_basis: median of 48 chart rows (R/settled thickness, R-19+), computed

materials.name: Loose-fill (blown) cellulose (new)
materials.note: Computed as R / minimum settled thickness from GreenFiber charts (rows R-19 and up). Building America basement guide: cellulose R-3 to 4 per inch. Cellulose settles: charts give both initial installed and settled thickness; install to the initial thickness.
materials.use_basis: median of 38 chart rows (R/settled thickness, R-19+), computed

materials.name: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) rigid board
materials.note: BSC/DOE Guide to Insulating Sheathing: 'Typically EPS foam has a rated value of approximately R-4 per inch.' Insulfoam R-Tech I TDS: 3.85 at 75 F. Retail 1 in EPS at Menards labelled R-4 (graphite EPS R-4.1). Use the labelled R of the board when known.

materials.name: Extruded polystyrene (XPS) rigid board
materials.note: R-5.0/in at 75 F (OC FOAMULAR NGX, DuPont ScoreBoard, Kingspan GreenGuard). OC also publishes higher values at colder mean temperatures (1 in = R-5.4 at 40 F). Building America wall guide gives a wider R-3.8-R-5.0/in for XPS.

materials.name: Polyisocyanurate (polyiso) rigid board, foil faced
materials.note: Retail 1 in boards are labelled R-6.0 (Rmax Thermasheath-3, JM AP Foil-Faced); DuPont Thermax 1 in = R-7.0. BSC guide: most polyiso has LTTR R-6.5 per inch (15-year weighted). Building America wall guide gives R-5.6-R-8/in. Polyiso R per inch is not linear with thickness (Rmax: 2 in = 13.1, 4 in = 27.4), so use the per-thickness table when available.

materials.name: Closed-cell spray polyurethane foam (~2 pcf)
materials.note: DOE 2009 guide lists 1 in closed-cell = R-6.5; Heatlok HFO Pro aged 7.4/in; DIY kits (Froth-Pak, Touch 'n Seal) R-6.2/in.

warning.text: Vermiculite may contain asbestos. EPA: vermiculite insulation is a 'pebble-like, pour-in product' 'usually gray-brown or silver-gold in color'; a mine near Libby, Montana supplied over 70 percent of US vermiculite from 1919 to 1990 and it was contaminated with asbestos (often sold as Zonolite). EPA says: 'YOU SHOULD ASSUME THE VERMICULITE CONTAINS ASBESTOS AND DO NOT DISTURB IT!' Do not store items in or let children play in such an attic, 'Do not attempt to remove the insulation yourself', and hire a professional asbestos contractor before remodeling that would disturb it. ENERGY STAR: 'Do not disturb vermiculite insulation unless you have had it tested by an approved lab' (contact your local health department for a lab).
warning.calculator_rule: If the user selects vermiculite, show the warning and do not recommend adding insulation on top without professional assessment.

materials_general_note.text: ENERGY STAR: most common types (fiberglass, cellulose, mineral wool) have an R-value of about 3-3.5 per inch; ENERGY STAR's attic diagrams assume R-3/inch. Quick check: if attic insulation is level with or below the floor joists, you probably need to add more.

loose_fill.chart_basis: Volumatic III, 3rd gear, 8 in gate; chart based on settled thickness; coverage can vary by as much as 10% with job conditions/equipment. Framing-adjusted columns are for 2x6 framing at 16 in o.c.
notes: Appears to be GreenFiber's current formulation (Rev K, May 2026). R-11/26/32/40/48/50 rows are not on Rev K.

GreenFiber's 2023 DIY guide (DM-6.3-38 Rev E 01-23) prints a 'Sanctuary (25 lb bag)' chart whose R-49 and R-60 rows differ (13.8 sq ft/bag, 72.6 bags; 10.8 sq ft/bag, 92.5 bags) and whose footnote cites a 22.55 lb nominal bag; prefer Rev K.

waste_factor.note: No authoritative published waste factor was found (the web search budget for this task was exhausted before retailer/manufacturer calculator guides could be located; Home Depot/Lowe's pages were blocked). Related sourced facts: GreenFiber says job conditions, technique and equipment 'can influence actual coverage by as much as 10%'; loose-fill charts give the MINIMUM bags per 1,000 sq ft and installers must meet both minimum bags and minimum thickness; batt bags must be rounded up to whole bags. Choose an editorial overage and label it as such.

framing_factor.note: GreenFiber: 'For maximum coverage per bag (adjusted for framing), the framing factor for 16" OC spacing is 9.375%; for 24" OC spacing the framing factor is 6.25%' (= 1.5 in framing / spacing). Loose-fill attic charts are NET coverage (no framing deduction) unless a framing-adjusted column is used.

stud_spacing_in.note: DOE Building America: batts are sized to fit framing cavities typically at 16 or 24 in on center (batts approximately 15 or 23 in wide). Full-width 16 in and 24 in batts (16x48, 24x48, 16x96, 24x96) are sold for attics/floors. Choosing 16 in as the UI default is an editorial choice.

batt_coverage_note.text: Batt bag 'sq ft' is the batt area (width x length x pieces; e.g., OC R-13 15x93 x 13 pcs = 125.94 sq ft). A 15 in batt fills one 16 in o.c. bay, so measured in gross wall area a bag covers about 16/15 (~1.07x) its labelled sq ft; for 24 in o.c. with 23 in batts about 24/23 (~1.04x). Computed, not a manufacturer statement.

cavity_depth_in.note: Actual depth of nominal lumber. 2x4 = 3.5 and 2x6 = 5.5 appear in GreenFiber and Owens Corning wall coverage charts; 2x8 = 7.25, 2x10 = 9.25, 2x12 = 11.25 appear in the Owens Corning ProPink L77 brochure (May 2024) cathedral-ceiling/floor framing rows.

attic_joist_depth_in.note: No source was found for which ceiling-joist size is most common. Depth values per cavity_depth_in. ENERGY STAR quick check: insulation level with or below the attic floor joists means you probably need more.

compressed_batt.text: Knauf: 'When R-19 6.25" is installed in a 2 x 6 cavity, the R-value will be R-18.' 2021 IECC: where insulation is installed in a cavity less than its label thickness, the installed (compressed) R-value must still meet the table value.

door_deduction_sqft.note: Benjamin Moore's online paint calculator subtracts 21 sq ft per door (formula in page code: 2*L*H + 2*W*H - 21*doors - 12*windows). 21 sq ft = a 3 ft x 7 ft door. Paint-calculator convention, not an insulation standard.

window_deduction_sqft.note: Benjamin Moore's paint calculator subtracts 12 sq ft per window. The ~15 sq ft (3 ft x 5 ft) convention mentioned in the brief could not be verified from a source in this research (search budget exhausted); treat 15 as unverified and prefer letting users enter window sizes.

loose_fill_rule.text: Owens Corning (AttiCat PDS): 'Stated R-value is achieved by installing the minimum required number of bags per 1,000 net sq. ft. at a thickness not less than the label minimum thickness.' GreenFiber: 'The applicator must install both the minimum number of bags per 1000 sq. ft. and the minimum installed thickness.' Bags needed = ceil(area_sqft / 1000 * bags_per_1000_sqft) (or area / sqft_per_bag), always rounded up.
